NFL schedule sample (2024-2025)

Source: R/data.R
nfl_schedules_sample.Rd

The complete 2024 and 2025 NFL schedule, trimmed to the game-level schedule, rest, and venue columns used by the package's analytics. Bundled so examples and tests run with no network access.

Usage

nfl_schedules_sample

Format

A tibble with 570 rows and 17 variables:

game_id

Game identifier (nflverse convention, e.g. "2024_01_BAL_KC").

season

Season year.

game_type

Game type: "REG", "WC", "DIV", "CON", or "SB".

week

Week number within the season.

gameday

Game date as an ISO 8601 string; coerce with as.Date().

gametime

Scheduled kickoff time in U.S. Eastern time ("HH:MM").

home_team

Three-letter home team abbreviation.

away_team

Three-letter away team abbreviation.

home_score

Final home-team score.

away_score

Final away-team score.

home_rest

Days of rest for the home team entering the game.

away_rest

Days of rest for the away team entering the game.

spread_line

Closing home-team spread; positive means the home team was favored.

location

"Home" or "Neutral".

div_game

1 if a divisional matchup, else 0.

stadium_id

Venue identifier, joinable to nfl_stadiums.

stadium

Venue name, joinable to nfl_stadiums.

Source

Retrieved with nflreadr::load_schedules(seasons = 2024:2025); see data-raw/process_data.R for the build script and venue overrides.

Details

stadium_id is the venue the game was actually played in, including the 15 neutral-site games (12 international, two Super Bowls, and one wildfire relocation). location flags neutral sites, so travel functions know both teams flew. Note gameday is stored as an ISO 8601 character string, not a Date, and gametime is Eastern time rather than venue local time. Together they support date-aware body-clock calculations.

Examples

nfl_schedules_sample
#> # A tibble: 570 x 17
#>    game_id         season game_type  week gameday   gametime home_team away_team
#>    <chr>            <int> <chr>     <int> <chr>     <chr>    <chr>     <chr>    
#>  1 2024_01_BAL_KC    2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 20:20    KC        BAL      
#>  2 2024_01_GB_PHI    2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 20:15    PHI       GB       
#>  3 2024_01_PIT_ATL   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    ATL       PIT      
#>  4 2024_01_ARI_BUF   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    BUF       ARI      
#>  5 2024_01_TEN_CHI   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    CHI       TEN      
#>  6 2024_01_NE_CIN    2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    CIN       NE       
#>  7 2024_01_HOU_IND   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    IND       HOU      
#>  8 2024_01_JAX_MIA   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    MIA       JAX      
#>  9 2024_01_CAR_NO    2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    NO        CAR      
#> 10 2024_01_MIN_NYG   2024 REG           1 2024-09-~ 13:00    NYG       MIN      
#> # i 560 more rows
#> # i 9 more variables: home_score <int>, away_score <int>, home_rest <int>,
#> #   away_rest <int>, spread_line <dbl>, location <chr>, div_game <int>,
#> #   stadium_id <chr>, stadium <chr>

# Regular-season games with the largest rest disparity
subset(
  nfl_schedules_sample,
  game_type == "REG" & home_rest - away_rest >= 7
)
